statements.body: A community garden group is the intended user of this project.
The group is experiencing organizational problems that cause friction among members.
Members are missing important information, tasks, or events because no adequate shared organizational system currently exists.
What specific types of things are being missed — tasks, schedules, announcements, resource bookings, or something else?
How many people are in the community garden group?
What tools, if any, does the group currently use to organize, and why are they insufficient?

concerns.coverage: The group experiences friction caused by members missing things, but the specific nature of what is missed and what currently happens without the project is not yet stated.
Users are members of a community garden group; count, technical comfort level, and individual roles within the group are not yet known.

candidates.body: Walk me through what happens today when something needs to get organized — for example, who announces a work day, how members find out, and where things fall through?
candidates.whySelected: Workflow is an uncovered core concern, and understanding the current end-to-end path — where information enters, who touches it, and where it gets dropped — simultaneously sharpens the vague problem statement and bounds what the first slice must capture. It also naturally surfaces answers to the ledgered unknowns about what is being missed and what tools are used today.

candidates.body: What specific types of things are members missing — tasks, schedules, announcements, plot assignments, or resource bookings?
candidates.whySelected: This resolves an already-ledgered unknown and converts a vague problem into a concrete one; the answer directly determines what the first vertical slice must handle.

candidates.body: How would you know, a couple of months after adopting this tool, that it actually reduced the friction — what would you see happening or stop happening?
candidates.whySelected: Success is an uncovered core concern; without observable evidence of improvement the framing cannot be judged done. However, it bounds the first slice less than understanding the workflow does.

readyAdvice.why: Two core concerns (workflow and success) are entirely uncovered, and three ledgered unknowns — what is being missed, group size, and current tools — remain unanswered. The problem is still too vague to bound a first vertical slice.

statements.body: The primary source of friction is that shared chores — specifically watering and composting — are being skipped.
Chores are skipped because members do not know whose turn or week it is to perform them.
A rotating or scheduled assignment system for watering and composting duties would resolve the core coordination gap.

concerns.coverage: The concrete pain is skipped watering and composting chores caused by unclear ownership of weekly duty assignments; members miss their turns because no visible schedule exists.
Work items are recurring chore duties (watering, composting); the handoff mechanism — who is assigned for a given week — is currently missing or invisible to members.

candidates.body: What observable change would tell the group the chore schedule is working — for example, watering and composting happening every week without reminders, or fewer complaints at meetings?
candidates.whySelected: Success is the only uncovered core concern, and the ledger already contains a decided approach (a rotating assignment system); defining the observable evidence of success now lets the first slice be judged rather than argued about.

candidates.body: How many members are in the group and how comfortable are they with digital tools like phones or shared apps?
candidates.whySelected: Group size and technical comfort are recorded unknowns that directly shape whether the first slice is a paper board, a group chat bot, or an app — it bounds the delivery medium of the rotation schedule.

candidates.body: Who will maintain the rotation schedule when members join, leave, or swap weeks?
candidates.whySelected: A rotating assignment system has been ratified, but no operator is named; an unowned schedule recreates the original invisibility problem the project exists to solve.

readyAdvice.why: The problem, users, and workflow gap are well established and a solution direction is ratified, but success has no observable definition yet and the group's size and current tooling remain open unknowns, so the first slice cannot yet be judged or sized.

statements.body: Success is defined as watering no longer being skipped and members no longer claiming they did not see the chore announcement.
Composting chores are implicitly included in the success condition, since the core problem named both watering and composting, but the user's answer only explicitly mentioned watering.

concerns.coverage: The group will consider the project working when watering stops being skipped and members stop claiming they never saw the schedule or announcement; explicit mention of composting in the success signal is unconfirmed.

candidates.body: How do members currently receive group information — a group chat, email list, physical notice board, or something else?
candidates.whySelected: The chosen fix is a visible rotating schedule, but the ledger says nothing about the channel members actually check. The delivery channel determines whether the first slice is a shared spreadsheet, a chat-bot reminder, or a laminated board, so this single answer bounds the build more than anything else still open.

candidates.body: Should the success condition explicitly include composting no longer being skipped, or is watering alone the measure that matters?
candidates.whySelected: An approved statement flags that composting was only implicitly included in the success definition. Ratifying or rejecting that inference resolves the one live tension in the ledger and keeps the success signal honest.

candidates.body: How many members share the watering and composting rotation?
candidates.whySelected: Group size is an approved unknown and shapes rotation design: a five-person rotation can be a note on a board, while a forty-person one needs real scheduling. It bounds the slice but less sharply than knowing the communication channel.

contradictions.summary: The stated problem names both watering and composting as the skipped chores, but the approved success condition explicitly mentions only watering; whether composting is inside the success measure is an unratified inference.

readyAdvice.why: All core concern codes have some coverage and the problem, workflow gap, and success signal are well framed, but the first slice cannot be shaped yet: the delivery channel members actually check, the group size, and whether composting is in scope for success are all unresolved, and any of them could change what gets built first.

candidates.body: Where would members most reliably see a weekly chore assignment — a group chat they already use, email, a physical board at the garden, or somewhere else?
candidates.whySelected: The core problem is that assignments are invisible, so the first slice succeeds or fails on the delivery channel members actually check. Knowing the channel bounds the slice tightly: it decides whether this is a printed rota, a chat-bot message, or a small web page, and it directly targets the success signal of members no longer claiming they did not see the announcement.

candidates.body: What tools does the group currently use to coordinate — a group chat, email list, paper sign-up sheet — and where do those break down?
candidates.whySelected: This is an already-approved unknown in the ledger. Answering it reveals both the constraint environment (what members will tolerate) and why prior coordination failed, which prevents building a schedule that repeats the same failure mode.

candidates.body: How many members are in the community garden group?
candidates.whySelected: This is an approved unknown. Group size shapes the rotation design (a five-person rota differs from a fifty-person one) and whether manual assignment is viable, but it bounds the slice less directly than the delivery channel does.

readyAdvice.why: Core concerns are covered and success is observable, but the first slice cannot be scoped until we know where members will actually see the schedule and what tools they already use. One or two more answers on channel and current tooling should make the seed slice-ready.
